Drugs that prolong the QTc interval, such as hydroxychloroquine sulfate, can increase the risk of Torsades de Pointes or sudden death, especially when combined with other QTc-prolonging drugs, in the presence of bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, or congenital QT prolongation. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate enhances immunosuppressive effects, while echinacea reduces them, potentially altering the risk of infection. The interaction's effect is unclear, so caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Etrasimod and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both increase each other's effects on the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Etrasimod may transiently decrease heart rate and delay AV conduction upon initiation, increasing the risk of QT prolongation and Torsades de Pointes when co-administered with Class Ia or Class III antiarrhythmic drugs or other QT-prolonging agents. 4. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are required, especially since QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 5. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and gepirone both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 6. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the effects of the influenza virus vaccine (trivalent, recombinant) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised, as the immune response to the vaccine may be diminished in immunocompromised individuals. 7. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate enhances the effects of insulin aspart and other antidiabetic drugs, increasing the risk of hypoglycemia. Dosage adjustments for insulin and other antidiabetic drugs may be necessary. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 8. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate increases the effects of various insulin formulations (e.g., insulin aspart protamine, insulin degludec, insulin glargine, insulin glulisine, insulin isophane human, insulin regular human, and inhaled insulin) by enhancing antidiabetic drug effects, raising the risk of hypoglycemia. Dosage reductions for insulin and other antidiabetic drugs may be required. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and isavuconazonium sulfate both reduce immunosuppressive effects, potentially increasing the risk of infection. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 10. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate increases immunosuppressive effects, while maitake reduces them, potentially altering the risk of infection. The interaction's effect is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and mavorixafor both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation, and dose reduction or discontinuation may be required in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. 12. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and mercaptopurine both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate decreases methotrexate levels, possibly by reducing renal clearance, though the exact mechanism is unknown. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 14. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and osilodrostat both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and ozanimod both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Co-administration with immunosuppressive therapies may increase the risk of additive immune effects during therapy and in the weeks following administration. 16. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and ponesimod both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Caution and monitoring are advised, especially when switching from drugs with prolonged immune effects to avoid unintended additive immunosuppressive effects. 17. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate decreases the effects of sipuleucel-T through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 18. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate increase the toxicity of hydroxychloroquine sulfate by prolonging the QTc interval. Pre-dose and post-colonoscopy ECGs should be considered in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 19. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and tobramycin inhaled both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Concurrent or sequential use should be avoided to reduce the risk of ototoxicity. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 20. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and ublituximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 21. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and valbenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and voclosporin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate decreases the effects of the zoster vaccine recombinant through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised, as immunosuppressive therapies may reduce the vaccine's effectiveness. 24. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of hydroxychloroquine sulfate by prolonging the QTc interval. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 25. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate increases praziquantel levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 26. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate does not appear to adversely affect antibody responses to the yellow fever vaccine, despite inhibiting its replication in vitro. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 27. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and adagrasib both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of Torsades de Pointes, other serious arrhythmias, and sudden death. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If unavoidable, more frequent monitoring is recommended. 28. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and adalimumab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 29. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and albuterol both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 30. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and alefacept both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 31. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and alfuzosin both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 32. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and amiodarone both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 33. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and amisulpride both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administered. 34. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and amitriptyline both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 35. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and amoxapine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 36. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and anagrelide both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 37. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and anakinra both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 38. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate decreases the effects of the anthrax vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. 39. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and antithymocyte globulin (equine or rabbit) both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 40. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and apomorphine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 41. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and arformoterol both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 42. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and aripiprazole both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 43. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and arsenic trioxide both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 44. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and artemether both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 45. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 46. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and asenapine (including transdermal formulations) both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 47. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate increases immunosuppressive effects, while astragalus decreases them, potentially altering the risk of infection. The interaction's effect is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 48. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and atomoxetine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 49. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and axicabtagene ciloleucel both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 50. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and azathioprine both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 51. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and azithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 52. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and basiliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 53. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine live through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. 54. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and bedaquiline both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 55. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and brexucabtagene autoleucel both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 56. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and bupivacaine implant may increase the risk of methemoglobinemia when co-administered with drugs that also cause methemoglobinemia. Caution and monitoring are advised. 57. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and buprenorphine (including buccal formulations) both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used.
